findings.rationale: HI's local model performance is far below the federation (AUC 0.66 vs pooled 0.80; ECE 0.086), with observed outcomes running well above predicted risk (CITL -0.078, observed prevalence 0.205 vs mean prediction 0.127). Its updates are anomalous: mean cosine to the median update is -0.48 (z=-6.1) and the min cosine is -0.81, with an update-norm outlier pattern. Subgroup outcomes show observed/expected ratios of 1.7 (Sex=0) and 1.6 (Sex=1) with no feature drift (max shift_sd about 0.2 and no onset). A low AUC with positive-label excess is the signature of flipped outcome labels rather than a prevalence shift alone. Persistent across rounds in the drift per-round table, so onset is taken as round 1.

UT has the weakest local discrimination in the federation (AUC 0.634, z=-5.2) with observed prevalence 0.177 against mean prediction 0.113 (CITL -0.063, z=-3.8) and high ECE (0.079, z=+3.6). Its uploaded update points against the federation median (mean cos -0.50, z=-6.2) with a median update norm about 2.8x the median client. Subgroup outcomes show observed/expected of 1.85 for Sex=0 (FNR z=6.07) and 1.49 for Sex=1, i.e. excess recorded positives not explained by the features and no feature drift. This matches flipped labels rather than a drift or subgroup-specific under-diagnosis pattern. Per-round CITL has been negative since early rounds.

NE shows low local AUC (0.655, z=-4.7) with observed prevalence 0.215 against mean prediction 0.149 (CITL -0.065, z=-3.9) and high ECE (0.075, z=+3.3), the same discrimination-loss plus positive-excess pattern as label noise. Its update is anomalous: median norm ratio about 3.0 and mean cosine -0.45 (z=-5.9). Subgroup outcomes show observed/expected 1.41 for Sex=1 and 2.36 for Income group 5, with no feature drift. Confidence is somewhat lower than for HI and UT because NE's per-round CITL was closer to zero in the first rounds, so onset could be a few rounds later, but the faulty pattern is present at the final round.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with updates, local performance, drift, feature-tail and subgroup views, then confirmed suspicions with a narrower drift query. Three clients (HI, UT, NE) stand out on several independent tools at once: anomalous updates (negative cosine to the median, large norm), low local AUC with observed prevalence above predicted risk, and subgroup observed/expected ratios well above 1 with no feature drift. The pattern matches flipped outcome labels (label_noise) rather than poisoning, since their local data and performance are abnormal. Not reported: GU (CITL z=-3.4 only), AL (BMI sd outlier, z_noise -3.1), CT (GenHlth p99 z_noise 6.1, uncorroborated by any other tool), and WV/ND/NM/PR feature outliers, which are single-statistic leads from small clients. Drift, prevalence and missing-artefact screens were clean for the remaining clients. Budget fully spent (20.0).
